units.translation: [ἀλάστορος [of the avenger]. On this form the Homeric Epimerisms in Cramer's Anecdota Oxoniensia vol. 1 p. 62, 12: παρὰ τὸ ἀλαστῶ ῥῆμα ἀλάστωρ ὁ Ζεὺς ἐπὶ τῶν χαλεπόν τι πρασσόντων, παρῆκται δὲ ἡ εὐθεῖα παρὰ τὴν ἀλάστορος γενικήν [from the verb alastō, alastōr is Zeus in the case of those doing something grievous, and the nominative is derived from the genitive alastoros]. Aeschylus in Ixion (fr. 90) πρευμενὴς ἀλάστορος [gracious avenger]. Another example from Aeschylus was adduced by the grammarian in Bekker's Anecdota p. 382, 30: αλάστορον ἀντὶ τοῦ ἀλάστορα, ἀπὸ τῆς εὐθείας ὁ ἀλάστορος [alastoron for alastora, from the nominative ho alastoros]. Aeschylus said “μέγαν ἀλάστορον” [great avenger]. Comparing these, Nauck conjectured that the words of the former grammarian should be restored as follows: Aeschylus in Ixion “μέγαν ἀλάστορον” [great avenger] and elsewhere “πρευμενῶς ἀλάστορον” [graciously an avenger], from Eumenides 236 “δέχου δὲ πρευμενῶς ἀλάστορον” [receive graciously the avenger], where now ἀλάστορα [avenger] is read, the next verse beginning with οὐ [not].

and from the father's side an avenger would be a helper.
we shall make the all-destroying god, the heavy avenger, our housemate.

but he would provide you a prize still more painful than this.
